subject: math
cluster: Understand and apply theorems about circles
intro: All circles are similar to one another. Given any two circles, you can map one exactly onto the other by a translation (to line up the centers) followed by a dilation (to match the radii). The dilation's scale factor is the ratio of the radii. Because a single shape, the circle, differs only by position and size, every circle has the same shape, so they are all similar. This is why formulas like circumference $=2\pi r$ and area $=\pi r^2$ have the same form for every circle.

items.prompt: Circle $A$ has radius $3$ and circle $B$ has radius $12$. What dilation scale factor maps $A$ onto $B$?

steps: The scale factor is the ratio of the target radius to the original radius.
So a dilation with scale factor $4$ maps $A$ onto $B$.

items.prompt: What two transformations map any circle onto any other circle?

steps: First line up the centers with a translation.
Then match the radii with a dilation.
So a translation followed by a dilation works.
Any circle can be carried onto any other by a translation and a dilation.
That is exactly what it means for figures to be similar.
solution.answer: Because a translation and a dilation map any circle onto any other.

steps: Every circle maps onto every other by rigid motion + dilation.
So yes, all circles are similar.

items.prompt: What is the dilation scale factor from a circle of radius $2$ to one of radius $10$?

steps: Scale factor is the ratio of radii.

items.prompt: What transformation lines up the centers of two circles?

steps: Moving one center onto another is a slide.
